events.title: Formation of the Soviet Union
events.description: The First Congress of Soviets in Moscow ratified the treaty creating the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics, uniting the Russian, Ukrainian, Belarusian, and Transcaucasian Soviet republics into a single federal state.
events.significance: The USSR became one of the world's two superpowers, shaping global politics, the Second World War, and the Cold War until its dissolution in 1991.

events.title: Birth of Rudyard Kipling
events.description: Rudyard Kipling, the English novelist and poet, was born in Bombay, British India. He later wrote The Jungle Book, Kim, and the poem 'If—'.
events.significance: Kipling became one of the most popular writers of the British Empire and in 1907 became the first English-language writer to receive the Nobel Prize in Literature.

events.title: Gadsden Purchase Signed
events.description: The United States signed an agreement with Mexico to buy about 29,670 square miles of land in present-day southern Arizona and New Mexico, negotiated by James Gadsden.
events.significance: The purchase established the final continental borders of the contiguous United States and provided a southern route for a transcontinental railroad.

events.title: Execution of Saddam Hussein
events.description: Saddam Hussein, the former president of Iraq, was executed by hanging in Baghdad after being convicted by an Iraqi court of crimes against humanity for the 1982 killing of 148 Shia villagers in Dujail.
events.significance: His execution marked the end of the former dictator's era, but it was controversial and highlighted deep sectarian divisions in post-invasion Iraq.

events.title: Israel and the Vatican Establish Diplomatic Relations
events.description: Israel and the Holy See signed the Fundamental Agreement, committing to full diplomatic relations and addressing the legal status of the Catholic Church in Israel.
events.significance: The agreement ended decades without formal ties and marked a milestone in Catholic-Jewish relations following the Second Vatican Council's reforms.
